title: Fixed-head candidate self-convergence independent of finite Reference
scientific_question: Do the frozen Layer-ROM candidate trajectories themselves converge under the existing dt-halving ladder, independently of whether their distance to the finite Reference trajectory decreases?

trigger.reason: Reference-relative error did not show a common monotone temporal signature, so candidate self-convergence must be separated from finite-Reference discrepancy before changing closure or state.

scope.boundary: fixed zero pressure head at 160 cm, zero top flux
scope.closure: unchanged standard LARE internal closure plus BC1 zero-head bottom closure

temporal_ladder.integrator: same source-anchored iterative Heun route used in B1HCG

pairwise_self_differences.coarse_mid: dt=1e-4 trajectory minus dt=5e-5 trajectory at common observation times
pairwise_self_differences.mid_fine: dt=5e-5 trajectory minus dt=2.5e-5 trajectory at common observation times

component_classification.SATURATED: both coarse-mid and mid-fine RMS self-differences are <= 1e-12
component_classification.CONVERGING: not SATURATED and mid-fine RMS self-difference is strictly smaller than coarse-mid
component_classification.apparent_order: log2(coarse-mid RMS / mid-fine RMS), diagnostic only when both are positive

material_decision.SELF_CONVERGENT: all five causal-core components are CONVERGING or SATURATED and at least one is CONVERGING

interpretation_rules: If R16_OP is self-convergent while its Reference-relative residual from B1HCG persists or grows, the frozen Layer-ROM integrator is numerically settling but not toward the finite Reference trajectory. This does not by itself identify which trajectory is closer to the continuous Richards solution.
If R16_OP self-convergence is not established, further closure/state redesign is held because the research propagation route itself remains numerically unresolved.
No zero-dt extrapolated hydrological acceptance is computed.
R8 is reported only as secondary context and does not override the R16_OP primary decision.
